notes: The last honest gap in memory suppression is closed: a derived owner-profile item can now be forgotten. The owner profile derives keywords from session transcripts, and each one carried its own score contribution, trait, tier and coverage - items that reached the owner through the console, the proactive push and the search leg, and that no control could silence. Each keyword is now a source of its own with an opaque id, and the profile view offers the same forget action as the memory view: a read-only preview first, showing how many items would be silenced and whether the profile, the score and the coverage are affected, with the confirm button disabled until that preview arrives. A silenced item is excluded where the profile is built - so the stored document, the score, the traits, the tiers and the coverage tallies are computed without it and a re-analysis cannot bring it back - and where a stored profile is read, so the forget takes effect at the next read with no tick and no restart. The session transcript keeps the words: what is silenced is the derived item and its contribution, never the original text, and the console says exactly that where it offers the action. Two new gates cover the flow, one over real HTTP and one offline in a browser. The counts move with the feature: 2932 core assertions and 1895 locale keys per pack. No new credential, no new outbound path, no change to any shared gateway.
